Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". r02.

The premise is incorrect — this repository has no per-user API rate-limiting middleware.

I searched the Go backend broadly (`grep -rin "ratelimit|rate_limit|rate limit|throttle|limiter"` across `server/` and `internal/`) and found only a single mention: a doc comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86` listing "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" as an unimplemented consideration, not actual code.

I also inspected the API middleware/interceptor chain directly at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-137`, where the Connect/gRPC-Gateway interceptors are registered:
```go
connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
    NewMetadataInterceptor(),
    NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
)
```
This is the full interceptor/middleware stack for the API — metadata conversion, logging, panic recovery, and auth — with no rate-limiting step present, and no `net/http` rate-limit middleware wired in elsewhere (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, `server/router/rss/rss.go` were also checked and contain none).

So there are no configured request limits to report, per-user or otherwise, because the feature doesn't exist in this codebase.

## Findings

**1. Does per-user API rate-limiting middleware exist? NO.**

I searched the entire repository (this is the `usememos/memos` Go backend + React frontend) for `rate limit`, `rateLimit`, `rate_limit`, `RateLimiter`, `throttle`, `express-rate-limit`, `x/time/rate`, `429`/`TooManyRequests`, and middleware/interceptor registration sites. There is no rate-limiting middleware anywhere in the codebase — backend or frontend.

**2/3. Nothing to report** — no file defines it, no `app.use(...)`/interceptor chain registers it, and there are no configured limit values, because it doesn't exist.

**4. What actually exists (for an accurate premise-correction answer):**

- **No HTTP-layer rate limiting at all.** The middleware/interceptor stack is fully enumerated at:
  - `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:51-52` — Echo server only registers `middleware.Recover()` and a CORS middleware (`newCORSMiddleware`), nothing else.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-141` — the Connect-RPC interceptor chain: `NewMetadataInterceptor()`, `NewLoggingInterceptor()`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor()`, `NewAuthInterceptor()`. All four are defined in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`. None throttle requests — they handle header propagation, logging, panic recovery, and auth only.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69-97` — a `gatewayAuthMiddleware` wraps the gRPC-Gateway mux, again auth-only, no rate limiting.

- **Two concurrency semaphores exist, but these are NOT rate limiters** (no time window, not per-user, global across all users):
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59` — `thumbnailSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(3)` — limits to 3 concurrent thumbnail generations.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60` — `imageProcessingSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(2)` — limits to 2 concurrent EXIF-stripping operations.
  - Used at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_image.go:67-75` (`acquireImageProcessingSlot`) and consumed at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:158-160`, which returns `codes.ResourceExhausted, "too many image processing requests"` when the semaphore can't be acquired. This is a global in-flight-request cap, not a per-user or per-IP rate limit.

- `golang.org/x/time v0.15.0` appears in `go.mod:151` but only as an **indirect** (transitive) dependency — the `x/time/rate` package is never imported/used anywhere in the Go source (confirmed via grep for `golang.org/x/time/rate` across all `.go` files: zero matches). So even the standard Go rate-limiting library isn't actually wired up.

- Other unrelated "limit"/"too many" occurrences found are just batch-size validation guards (business logic, not rate limiting), e.g.:
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/instance_service.go:78` — max batch get instance settings
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:145` — max batch get usernames
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:355` — max batch delete attachments
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go:24` — max batch get link metadata
  - `/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go:97` — default page-size limit for loading attachments

- `/bench/home/work/internal/email/doc.go:86` contains only a **documentation comment/TODO**: `- Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse` — this is an aspirational note in a doc comment, not an implementation. No corresponding code exists.

- On the frontend (`web/src`), the only related hits are unrelated UI debouncing utilities: `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useDebouncedEffect.ts` and its usages in `MemoEditor` components (`useLinkMemo.ts`, `cacheService.ts`, `InsertMenu.tsx`) — these debounce local UI effects/autosave, not API request throttling, and are client-side only.

**Bottom line:** This repository has no per-user (or per-IP) API rate-limiting middleware. The closest things are (a) a documentation TODO mentioning email rate limiting that was never implemented, and (b) two small global concurrency semaphores (limits of 3 and 2 concurrent operations) guarding thumbnail/image-processing work, which cap simultaneous in-flight operations server-wide rather than limiting requests per user over a time window.</result>
